assertions.title: Click node navigates to entity detail

steps.observed: Graph page loaded with 50 nodes visible

assertions.title: Double-click node expands neighbors

steps.expected: Graph page loads with 50 nodes, 0 edges
API call to fetch relations, new edges/nodes appear
steps.observed: API call made to /api/entities/72096f09e0a0424db7c50a1e198e1860/relations, edge count increased from 0 to 1

assertions.notes: The neighbor entity (4225e7deb1d442f89f1137daa0750d9c) was already in the initial 50-node seed, so only an edge was added. This is correct behavior - the expansion logic adds new nodes only if the neighbor is not already present.

assertions.title: Drag node pins position

steps.observed: 2 nodes loaded with viewport transform matrix(3.38, 0, 0, 3.38, 307, 293)

steps.expected: Node stays at dropped position (not affected by force simulation)

assertions.notes: The focused graph (?focus=:id) was used because the default 50-node graph has very small nodes due to extreme zoom-out. The focused graph provides larger, more interactable nodes for drag testing.

assertions.title: Graph to entity detail

steps.observed: Graph page loaded with nodes visible

assertions.notes: This assertion is functionally identical to VAL-GRAPH-004 and was tested simultaneously.

frictions.description: Default 50-node graph renders at 10% zoom level, making nodes very small (12x4 pixels) and difficult to interact with via mouse events
frictions.resolution: Used ?focus=:id parameter to load a focused 2-node graph with larger, more interactable nodes (408x135 pixels)

frictions.description: Agent-browser's dblclick command did not trigger ReactFlow's onNodeDoubleClick handler reliably
frictions.resolution: Used mouse events (mouse move, mouse down, mouse up) with proper timing to simulate double-click

summary: Tested 4 assertions: all 4 passed. Graph node interactions (click, double-click, drag) work correctly. Navigation from graph to entity detail works. Double-click correctly fetches relations and adds edges (and new nodes if neighbors not already in graph). Drag correctly pins node position and prevents force simulation from moving it.
